title: Redwood discovery - model selection for Celeste AI
summary: Discovery with Celeste AI focusing on which open models to use and whether hosted/dedicated/private deployment makes sense given long-context requirements, multilingual UI, and tool-calling integrations. Customer cares about latency for chat, cost predictability, and security (SAML, KMS). SE to run a quick benchmark and share guidance on quantization/context and function-calling capabilities. Next step: provide pricing, security docs, and schedule a POC benchmarking slot.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood. quick roll call?
[00:07] Maya Rao: Maya here, VP of ML at Celeste.
[00:09] Tom Bennett: Tom, SRE.
[00:11] Lina Park: Lina, product.
[00:13] Oliver Wu: Oliver, data eng.
[00:17] Ethan Liu: Ethan from Redwood (SE) on the call.
[00:22] Sofia: Awesome. Agenda today: understand your workload, context length needs, multilingual use, tool calling, and deployment preference (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
[00:35] Maya: High level — we run a conversational assistant for enterprise customers, multi-lingual support across EN/ES/FR/DE/JP, sometimes Chinese. Typical sessions are long, several KBs of context, and we also call internal tools (customer DB, calendar) via function calls. Latency target is 300-600ms for token streaming on hosted endpoints, ideally, and cost is a concern.
[01:05] Ethan: ok so long context + tool-calling + multilingual, got it. can you give ballpark on context window sizes?
[01:12] Maya: for chat history + docs it's often 8k to 32k tokens; in rare cases 100k+ for full document context but we can truncate. For initial POC we'd like to validate 32k and 100k tradeoffs.
[01:30] Sofia: great, that pushes us to consider models with long-context support and likely dedicated or private if you need consistent latency at those windows. do you currently host inference anywhere?
[01:40] Tom: We run a mix — some models in-house on k8s with Triton for smaller models, and we use a third-party API for larger LLMs. Our infra team prefers VPC/VPN connectivity for audit reasons.
[01:52] Lina: product also wants tool calling to be straightforward — we call our customer DB and a calendar microservice; security is key, so we need tokens not leaking.
[02:02] Ethan: on tool-calling, Redwood supports function calling patterns and can run tool integrations with controlled I/O — we also surface audit logs and redaction options. For model selection: are you leaning open models vs hosted proprietary?
[02:16] Maya: Preference for open models due to cost and control, but we need parity on multilingual and tool behavior. Also, quantized models are attractive for cost but we worry about quality regressions.
[02:30] Sofia: totally. Rough guidance: for EN-heavy workloads and low latency: non-quantized 70B-class models or quantized 34B with careful eval. For 32k context windows you want models that were trained or adapted for long context; for 100k we usually recommend retrieval + chunking and KV cache plus an LLM variant that supports window extension.
[02:52] Oliver: can you name specific models we should evaluate?
[02:55] Ethan: sure — open models that customers commonly test: Llama 2 / Mistral / Mistral-Instruct forks, Mistral M05 / Llama-derivatives with long-context variants (e.g., LongLLaMA forks), and newer long-context open models like Orca-Infinite or Mistral-Long. Also for multilingual, models like GEMMA or XGen variants perform better. We can map tradeoffs: performance, memory, licensing.
[03:23] Maya: what about Hugging Face and running weights ourselves vs Redwood hosted?
[03:27] Sofia: if you need predictable throughput at scale and don't want to manage GPU fleets, Redwood Dedicated gives reserved capacity and autoscaling; Private gives VPC + on-prem if policies require no egress. Hosted is fastest to get started but has shared capacity and usage-based pricing.
[03:45] Tom: our security people asked about SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS integration. Do you support customer-managed KMS?
[03:54] Ethan: Yes for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. Dedicated can be configured with KMS in a VPC and we provide audit logs with token-level tracing. Hosted supports encrypted-at-rest and limited KMS options depending on plan; we can share SOC2 docs.
[04:10] Lina: back to model quality — tool-calling is critical. Do models vary a lot in how they handle function calls?
[04:16] Ethan: yes, some models interpret function schemas differently; we run a function-calling layer that standardizes call detection and validation. For open models, this is more of an engineering integration: fine-tuning or prompt templates plus a small validator can get consistent behavior.
[04:31] Maya: latency at 32k vs 8k — how does that impact cost and user experience?
[04:36] Sofia: longer contexts drive memory and compute; per-token latency tends to increase because of KV cache overhead and attention scaling. We recommend chunking + local retrieval + on-demand context stitching; cost increases linearly with length for most runtimes. Dedicated pools with larger GPUs (A100/H100-class) help keep latency lower at high windows.
[05:00] Oliver: are there Redwood-verified perf profiles we can look at?
[05:03] Sofia: yes, we can share our model catalog perf profiles that show throughput/latency at different sequence lengths and quantization states. I'll attach that.
[05:11] Tom: for the POC, can you run benchmarks with our sample workload? we can provide a 10k-session sample trace and a few prompt sets in EN/ES/FR.
[05:20] Ethan: yes, we typically spin up a dedicated benchmarking job — we can run hosted quick tests but for realistic latency we prefer Dedicated test slots or Private where possible. For initial model shortlist we can run 3-4 models at 8k and 32k, and then a focused 100k approach using retrieval.
[05:38] Maya: about quantization — we worry about hallucinations and instruction following after int8/4 quant. how do you advise?
[05:44] Ethan: quantization is model-dependent. Some models survive aggressive quant well; others need qlora or fine-tuning to preserve instruction following. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and run automated evals on your prompt sets to detect regressions.
[05:58] Lina: multilingual: do you recommend a single multilingual model or language-specific models?
[06:03] Sofia: tradeoff — one multilingual model simplifies deployment but may underperform some specialized weights. If you need parity across many languages, a multilingual 70B-class or dedicated translation pipeline plus a base model is common. We can evaluate per-language metrics from your sample.
[06:20] Oliver: any licensing pitfalls with Llama 2 / Mistral for commercial use?
[06:24] Ethan: Llama 2 is permissive for many use cases but you must comply with Meta's license; Mistral's permissive OK but check model-specific restrictions. We'll surface licensing notes in the doc pack.
[06:35] Maya: are there recommended rollouts — can we canary models or fall back to smaller models for cheap queries?
[06:40] Sofia: yes, Redwood supports routing policies: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants based on latency/cost thresholds. You can route by user tier or workload.
[06:52] Tom: for the POC, we require RBAC and audit traces tied to our IDP.
[06:56] Ethan: Private plus Dedicated both support SSO/SAML and RBAC. Hosted supports SSO for enterprise tiers and detailed audit logs for routes; we'll provide exact retention and formatting in the security packet.
[07:10] Lina: timeline — we ideally want a POC in 3 weeks to evaluate quality at 32k and latency.
[07:15] Sofia: that's tight but doable. Steps: (1) send pricing + perf profiles + security doc, (2) Celeste sends sample traces and prompt set, (3) Redwood spins benchmark (hosted quick run + dedicated test slot), (4) review results and pick model for pilot.
[07:31] Maya: can you also show cost estimates — per 1M tokens with 32k windows vs trimmed retrieval?
[07:36] Ethan: yes we'll produce unit economics scenarios: hosted vs dedicated pricing, plus projected savings from caching/batching/quantization.
[07:45] Oliver: any limitations on tool calling when using quantized models or long windows?
[07:50] Ethan: function calling is orthogonal but long windows increase parsing latency; with quantization you may see subtle differences in text generation that affect detection heuristics — our function-calling layer includes validators to reduce false positives/negatives.
[08:05] Sofia: ok, I want to clarify deliverables. Ethan will run bench; I'll send pricing and perf profiles; security will send SOC2 + SAML/KMS docs. Celeste will send data and a primary contact.
[08:18] Maya: primary contact will be Oliver for data and Tom for infra.
[08:22] Lina: product will join demo/benchmark review.
[08:25] Sofia: any other blockers?
[08:27] Maya: legal asked about data residency — some EU customers require EU-only processing. Is Private available in EU?
[08:34] Ethan: yes, Private deployments can be on-prem or in a VPC in EU regions. Dedicated can be provisioned in EU with isolated pools. Hosted region availability varies but we'll map it out.
[08:47] Tom: can you share a sample benchmark script so we know what to expect?
[08:50] Sofia: we'll attach the benchmarking harness and a checklist for the POC.
[08:56] Maya: great, thanks.
[08:57] Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and timeboxed benchmarks.
[09:03] (call ends)
